questions: Should the histogram be normalized (density=True) or show raw frequencies (density=False)?
When data is empty or has only one unique value, should the normal curve be omitted, but should the histogram still be plotted (potentially empty)?
For duplicate counting, should 'duplicate' include the first occurrence (i.e., keep=False) or only subsequent repeats (keep='first'/'last')?
If the data contains NaN values in the 'value' column, how should they be handled for duplicate counting and histogram fitting?
Should the normal distribution curve be plotted over the full x-axis range of the plot (xmin, xmax from plt.xlim()) or over a fixed range (e.g., data min/max)?
Is the 'bins' parameter intended for the histogram only, or should it also influence the normal curve (e.g., curve resolution)?
Should the function raise an error if the 'value' column is missing from the DataFrame, or handle it gracefully (e.g., return empty Counter and empty plot)?

If the data has only one unique value but multiple occurrences, should the histogram show a single bar (since density=True may produce a spike), and should the x-axis limits be set to include that value?
